title: Harbour: parseParkedWait reads the newest state-bearing entry, skipping tool/usage/resources/[ticket]/stamps
description:
Repo: JKershaw/LinearViewer (Harbour)

Piece 2 of 2 of **LIN-4233** (parent). The parent's description holds the full approved plan ("Implementation Plan", section "Piece 2 — Harbour (LinearViewer): one way to read a park") and the Scope decision of 4 Nov. The approving review's builder notes are in its comment thread (comment 66095182-6633-46a1-9090-19f46d23a27f) and are folded in below. Read both there; this is this piece's slice.

**Starting point:** the parent's approved plan is where this piece starts. Follow it, and where the code shows it is wrong, change course and say so on LIN-4233.

Session fit: fits one session
Plan-review due: no — covered by LIN-4233's approving plan-review (comment 66095182-6633-46a1-9090-19f46d23a27f, rev 2)
Grounding commits: LinearViewer `476d9ad4` (still `origin/main` at breakdown, 4 Nov 22:40 UTC; nothing has landed on the touched files since); simple-dispatcher `bf499a4`.

**Lands after** the simple-dispatcher order subtask (blocked-by). That piece's system-tier proof needs today's reader to go red and then green on the producer swap alone.

## What this piece does

`parseParkedWait` (`lib/session-telemetry.js:324`) stops treating the literal latest entry as decisive. It decides on the newest entry that is **a statement about the session's state**, so a trailing entry from any process can't hide a park.

## Implementation (pruned at close-out)

Implemented as approved in LinearViewer PR [https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2280](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2280>) (merged as `279dcb0a`, deployed): `_isNonStateEntry` beside `DECISION_LIFECYCLE_STAMP_KINDS` skips `tool`/`usage`/`resources`, legacy untagged `[usage]`, decision stamps (via `_isStampEntry`) and `[ticket]` markers (via `TICKET_PREFIX`); the `since` walk uses the same predicate; `findWakeEvent` is not shared; the census was re-run with no new trailing kind. One deliberate deviation: `decision-lifecycle-stamp-drift.test.js` now pins the `_isStampEntry` call through `_isNonStateEntry`. The simple-dispatcher pointers were rewritten in PR [https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/327](<https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/327>). The full pre-prune text is in the task snapshots and the comment trail.

## Witnesses (`tests/unit/session-telemetry.test.js`; 1–5 red before, green after)

1. park, then `kind:'tool'` → parked
2. park, then `kind:'usage'` → parked; also a legacy untagged `[usage]` line; also park, then `kind:'resources'` → parked
3. park, then a tool, then a stamp → parked
4. park, then `{kind:'status', message:'[ticket] LIN-1 done'}` → parked (the reaper's exact shape)
5. park, a tool relay, another park → one run, `since` at the first park; and the same with a ticket marker in place of the tool relay
6. Guards that must stay true:
   * park, `assistant-text`, park → two runs
   * park, `[done]` → not parked
   * park, an untagged `[working] … alive` heartbeat → not parked
   * park, `[ticket]` marker, `[done]` → not parked
   * (review note 2) park, then `{kind:'heartbeat', message:'[working · verifying] verifying in background (scheduled wakeup) · idle 2m · next heartbeat in ≤1m'}` → still parked, with `latest` advanced

## Stale text to rewrite

Each should say the reader scans back past entries that are not about session state:

* `parseParkedWait`'s own docblock ("Only the LATEST feedback entry decides"). Name the skip set, and say that a trailing kind which is neither listed nor state-bearing still hides a park (accepted limit).
* `lib/render-run-steps.js:325-336`: rewrite the **whole** parenthetical, including the "trailing-`[usage]`" note and "tracked separately". This task is that fix (review note 4).
* `routes/dashboard-feed.js:180-184` ("only from the run's own latest feedback text").
* `docs/dispatch-integration.md:493-495`.

## Acceptance criteria

* Witnesses 1–5 were seen red on `476d9ad4` and are green after; witness 6 is green before and after. Harbour's unit suite passes in CI.
* A parked session followed by trailing tool, usage, legacy `[usage]`, resources and `[ticket]` entries reads as parked. Finished and progressing sessions still don't.
* Confirm that simple-dispatcher's `postTicketMarkerDelta` caveat and the F2 comment (written by the sibling piece to point at this subtask) are now true. If their wording needs a change once this lands, make it a one-line simple-dispatcher follow-up and say so on LIN-4233.
* The stale text above is rewritten.

## Follow-up, listed not filed

A positive "is a state statement" list for the reader, which needs a census of what real feedback holds.

**Blocked by:** LIN-4239 (simple-dispatcher order + Harbour-reader proof).

parent.title: simple-dispatcher: a parked or failed session's status is the last thing it posts, even with tool activity relayed

comments.body:
**Blocker check: resolved. LIN-4240 is unblocked and ready to implement.**

The only blocker was LIN-4239 (the `blocks` relation is already recorded). It has landed:
- simple-dispatcher PR https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/326 is **MERGED** (merged 22:59:52Z as `796bc9d`, squash of the approved head `f50679c`). The `unit tests` check is green on `f50679c`. `origin/main` is now `796bc9d`.
- So the ordering this piece had to wait for has happened. The sibling's `test/system/park-read.test.js` went red, then green against today's reader (LinearViewer `476d9ad4`) on the producer swap alone. Changing the reader now can't spoil that proof.
- LIN-4239 still says "In Progress" in Linear even though its PR is merged. That's only status bookkeeping (its Done gate is separate) and doesn't block this piece.

**Staleness re-check (ticket created 22:38:15Z):**
- LinearViewer `origin/main` moved `476d9ad4` → `950113b1` (LIN-4234, usage-snapshot-intake INVENTORY). `git log --since=2026-11-04T22:38:15Z` shows **no commits** touching `lib/session-telemetry.js`, `lib/render-run-steps.js`, `routes/dashboard-feed.js`, `docs/dispatch-integration.md`, `tests/unit/session-telemetry.test.js` or `tests/unit/decision-lifecycle-stamp-drift.test.js`. The line references and the plan still hold. Witnesses 1–5 can still be shown red on `476d9ad4` (or on `950113b1`, which is identical for these files).
- At `796bc9d`, simple-dispatcher holds the pointers this piece must make true: `hook.js:391` (the F2 comment), `test/ticket-marker-relay.test.js:439` and `docs/module-map.md:320`. Each says the reader skips `[ticket]` markers "once LIN-4240 lands". Check their wording against acceptance criterion 3 once this merges.

**Cost of doing nothing:** a reaper `[ticket]` marker, `[resources]` relay or tool relay landing after a park still hides it from Harbour's `parseParkedWait`. That leaves the parent LIN-4233 open with a known hole.

**Human needed?** No. Every question left is an engineering one, and the approved plan covers them.

**Next action:** dispatch an implementation session for LIN-4240 against LinearViewer `origin/main` (`950113b1`), following the description as written: skip predicate beside `DECISION_LIFECYCLE_STAMP_KINDS`, witnesses 1–6, the census re-run against `FEEDBACK_ENTRY_KINDS`, and the four stale-text rewrites.

**LIN-4240 done: PR open, CI green.** https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2280

- Commit `a829f909` on `feat/lin-4240-parked-wait-newest-state` (base `950113b1`).
- `parseParkedWait` now decides on the newest state-bearing entry: a new `_isNonStateEntry` predicate beside `DECISION_LIFECYCLE_STAMP_KINDS` skips `tool`/`usage`/`resources`, legacy untagged `[usage]`, decision stamps (via `_isStampEntry`) and `[ticket]` markers matched by `TICKET_PREFIX`. The `since` walk uses the same predicate. `findWakeEvent` is not shared.
- Witnesses 1–5 were red on the unfixed code and are green now; witness 6 guards were green before and after.
- Stale wording rewritten in the docblock, `lib/render-run-steps.js`, `routes/dashboard-feed.js` and `docs/dispatch-integration.md`.
- `npm run test:unit`: 23117 pass, 0 fail. `npm run test:hermetic:keyed`: 23117 pass, 0 fail, zero non-loopback sockets.
- CI on PR 2280: Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4, Secret scan and CI success all SUCCESS.
- Census: all producer kinds in simple-dispatcher are already in `FEEDBACK_ENTRY_KINDS` or the stamp set. No new trailing kind.
- Accepted limit: `evidence` and `decision` are not skipped, so a trailing one still hides a park.

## Review — LIN-4240

Reviewed PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2280 at head `a829f909` (base `950113b1`).

CI: green on `a829f909`. Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4, Secret scan (source) and CI success all passed (run 41931624625).

**Scope matches the plan.** The PR touches exactly the planned places: `lib/session-telemetry.js` (predicate + docblock), the three stale-text sites (`lib/render-run-steps.js`, `routes/dashboard-feed.js`, `docs/dispatch-integration.md`), the witnesses in `tests/unit/session-telemetry.test.js`, and an intentional update to `tests/unit/decision-lifecycle-stamp-drift.test.js`. That update is the "update that test on purpose" route the description allows. The `_isStampEntry` pin now follows the chain `parseParkedWait → _isNonStateEntry → _isStampEntry`. The "exactly three `decision-*` literals" assertion is unchanged and passes.

**How the code matches the constraints:**
- `PARKED_WAIT_SKIPPED_KINDS` and `_isNonStateEntry` sit right after `DECISION_LIFECYCLE_STAMP_KINDS` / `_isStampEntry`.
- `[ticket]` markers are matched on the message with `TICKET_PREFIX`, which is non-global, so `.test()` is safe. The forward reference is fine because the predicate only runs at call time.
- `findWakeEvent` is not shared.
- The `since` walk uses the same predicate.

**Independent checks I ran:**
- **Base red/green:** I ran the new test file with `lib/session-telemetry.js` reset to `950113b1`. All 8 witness tests for 1–5 fail. All 7 witness-6 guards pass. At `a829f909` the two touched test files pass 172/172.
- **Mutation checks.** Each mutation was applied on its own and reverted afterwards; each one turned exactly its own witnesses red:
  - Dropping `tool` from the kinds turns witnesses 1, 3 and 5 (tool) red.
  - Dropping `usage` turns witness 2 (usage) red. Dropping `resources` turns witness 2 (resources) red.
  - Removing the legacy untagged `[usage]` clause turns witness 2 (legacy) red.
  - Replacing `TICKET_PREFIX.test` with `false` turns witnesses 4 and 5 (ticket) red.
  - Removing the `_isStampEntry` call turns witness 3 red.
  - Reverting the `since` walk to stamp-only turns both witness-5 tests red.
  - Matching ticket markers by `kind==='status'` instead turns 3 guards red, including the non-matching `[ticket]` line and `[done]`.
- **Cross-repo proof:** I ran simple-dispatcher `test/system/park-read.test.js` (at `796bc9d`) with `HARBOUR_DIR` pointing at LinearViewer `a829f909`. It passed 3/3. That means the hook's real post shapes with every relay flag on still read as parked, blocked and failed.
- **Census re-run:** I ran `grep -n "kind: '" reapers.js heartbeat.js hook.js` at simple-dispatcher `796bc9d`. It found these feedback kinds: `assistant-text`, `tool`, `status`, `evidence`, `decision`, `decision-withdrawn`, `refusal`, `resources`, `heartbeat`. The `heartbeat.js` hits are wait-map kinds, not feedback. All are in `FEEDBACK_ENTRY_KINDS` or the stamp set, so there is no new trailing kind. Nothing in simple-dispatcher posts `[usage]` any more (LIN-4203), so the legacy skip only matters for historical data, which is correct.
- **Producer/reader regex parity:** simple-dispatcher's `TICKET_MARKER_LINE` (`transcript.js:354`) is byte-identical to Harbour's `TICKET_PREFIX`. `walkTicketMarkers` posts the trimmed line, so every reaper marker the producer emits matches the reader's skip.

**Regression check:** I ran `git log` on the touched files. The recent commits touching them are LIN-4203 (stopped posting `[usage]`, intake counts legacy snapshots) and the cost-read series. None of them is reverted or re-applied here. The LIN-3037 stamp skip is still in place, inside the predicate. No commits landed on the touched paths after the ticket was created (22:38:15Z).

**Isolated or one of a class?** I searched `lib/` and `routes/` for backward walks over `feedback[]`. The others (`findWakeEvent` and siblings in `lib/dispatch-terminal.js`, `lastWakeEntry` in `lib/run-view.js`, `_findLastDecision`/`_findDecisionAnswer` in `lib/digest-feedback.js`, `latestAssistantText` in `routes/dashboard.js`) all return the last *matching* entry, so a trailing relay can't hide anything from them. `recent-runs.js:39` uses `feedback.at(-1)` only for a timestamp. `parseParkedWait` was the only reader that decided on the literal-latest entry, so **this fix is isolated**. The accepted limit (a trailing `evidence`/`decision` still hides a park) is documented in the code and the docblock, as the plan says.

**Test level:** The unit witnesses match a pure function. The cross-module behaviour (producer posts → reader) is already covered at system tier by simple-dispatcher's `park-read.test.js`, which I re-ran against this head (above).

### What CI Did Not Prove
- **Inside (acceptance criterion 3, the simple-dispatcher pointers to this task). After the deploy (post-merge step):** after PR 2280 merges, these simple-dispatcher pointers become stale. Each still says the skip is in the future ("only once its sibling subtask LIN-4240 lands, so until then…"). Close-out should make a one-line simple-dispatcher follow-up commit/PR that rewrites them in the present tense, and say so on LIN-4233:
  - `hook.js:391-392`: should say that since LIN-4240, Harbour's `parseParkedWait` skips `[ticket]` markers, so a reaper marker after a park no longer hides it from that reader. The residual only matters to readers that key off the literal latest entry.
  - `test/ticket-marker-relay.test.js:439-440`: same present-tense rewrite. The assertion itself measures the producer's post order and stays as it is.
  - `docs/module-map.md:320`: change "that residual lands with LIN-4240, not here" to say that Harbour's reader skips such markers since LIN-4240.

  How to tell it's done: `grep -n "LIN-4240" hook.js test/ticket-marker-relay.test.js docs/module-map.md` in simple-dispatcher shows no "once/until … lands" wording.
- **Inside (cross-repo contract), settled before the merge:** the reader's skip set has to keep matching what simple-dispatcher actually posts (the `kind:'tool'`/`'resources'` tags and the `[ticket]` line shape). LinearViewer CI doesn't exercise that. I settled it by running `test/system/park-read.test.js` against `a829f909` (3/3 pass) and checking the regex is byte-identical. It is **discharged** for heads `a829f909` / `796bc9d`. Close-out only needs to re-run it if either head moves.

### Verdict
Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger. The reader change is complete. Every witness was independently shown red on base, green at head, and sensitive to mutation. CI is green. The only remaining item is the post-merge simple-dispatcher wording fix named above.

## Survey 1a (round 3)

**1. Why was this difficult?** It mostly wasn't. The code change was a predicate and two call sites. It bound in three places. First, `decision-lifecycle-stamp-drift.test.js` string-slices the source to check that `parseParkedWait`'s body literally calls `_isStampEntry(`. Moving the stamp check one level down broke that, so I had to rewrite the test on purpose. Second, `[ticket]` markers ride `kind:'status'`, so the predicate had to match on message text. That meant reaching `TICKET_PREFIX`, which is declared about 200 lines below the predicate: a forward reference that is safe at call time but a smell. Third, the stale prose: one sentence wrapped across comment lines, and the doc range named one stale sentence while a second sat ten lines lower. The real judgement was what counts as "state-bearing". I left `evidence` and `decision` decisive because the plan didn't list them.

**2. What would I have done first?** Looked at what real trailing entries look like in stored feedback, not only grepped the producers' `kind:` literals. The census told me which kinds exist, not which ones actually land after a park.

**3. What would I tidy?** I'd move `TICKET_PREFIX` above the predicate. I'd replace the source-slicing drift assertion with a behaviour test: a stamp after a park still reads as parked, and one already exists. As written, it pins the implementation's shape and will fire on any harmless refactor. I'd also trim my predicate's comment, which is longer than the code.

**4. If this area were how I'd want it:** each feedback kind would carry its role (state statement / relay / stamp) in one table beside `FEEDBACK_ENTRY_KINDS`. Ticket markers would have their own kind. Then this ticket would have been "classify `tool`, `usage`, `resources` as relays": a one-line table change with no message matching.

**5. What did the ticket get wrong?** Very little. Line references and grounding commits held. "Keep both true" for the drift test couldn't be done without a redundant call, though the ticket did allow updating it. The doc range under-counted the stale text.

**6. What did the change leave behind?**
- *Two places:* `PARKED_WAIT_SKIPPED_KINDS` now lives in `session-telemetry.js`, apart from `FEEDBACK_ENTRY_KINDS` in `dispatch-store.js`, and no test ties them. A newly allowed kind won't prompt anyone to classify it, and it will silently hide parks.
- *Something else should learn:* `findWakeEvent`/`run-view.js` has its own, deliberately unshared notion of noise, so there are now two readers with two skip rules.
- *Not updated:* simple-dispatcher's three "once LIN-4240 lands" pointers are now stale (noted on LIN-4233).
- *Simpler:* the render-run-steps caveat, the dashboard-feed comment and two doc sentences now describe the code as it is.

**7. Did the larger scope pay?** I can't see what the Survey recommended, so I'm judging from the work itself. The extra skip cases (resources, legacy `[usage]`, ticket markers) were nearly free: same predicate, a few witnesses. The ticket-marker skip is also what actually closes the cross-process race that LIN-4239 couldn't. The stale-text rewrites cost more time than the code but were worth doing, because they corrected a wrong mental model in four places. I'd draw the line at acceptance criterion 3, confirming simple-dispatcher's wording, which can't be settled until after merge. That belongs in a follow-up, not in this ticket's acceptance.

## Close-out — LIN-4240

**Merged.** LinearViewer PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2280, squash-merged as `279dcb0a`, pinned with `--match-head-commit a829f909` (the head CI passed on). `parseParkedWait` now decides on the newest state-bearing entry. It skips `tool`/`usage`/`resources`, a legacy untagged `[usage]` line, decision stamps and `[ticket]` markers (matched with `TICKET_PREFIX`). The `since` walk uses the same predicate. `findWakeEvent` is not shared.

**Review verdict:** Approve, conditional on the ledger. I made no fixes of my own to the LinearViewer PR; review asked for none there.

**CI.** LinearViewer CI is green on `a829f909`: Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4, Secret scan and CI success (run 41931624625). Post-merge CI on `main` (run 41933394508) also passed. The Railway deployment for `279dcb0a` ("Harbour / production") reached `success`.

**Ledger**
- *Inside, cross-repo contract (settled by review before merge).* Review ran simple-dispatcher `test/system/park-read.test.js` against `a829f909` (3/3) and checked that the `TICKET_MARKER_LINE` regex is byte-identical to `TICKET_PREFIX`. Neither head moved (`a829f909`, `796bc9d`), so I did not need to re-run it for the merge. I did re-run it on the deployed commit anyway: with `HARBOUR_DIR` at a worktree of `279dcb0a` it passes 3/3 against simple-dispatcher `796bc9d`.
- *Inside, post-merge simple-dispatcher wording (acceptance criterion 3).* Fixed in simple-dispatcher PR https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/327 (head `87f5b48`, squash-merged as `580a5ea`; `unit tests` check green, and `npm test` 4249 pass / 0 fail locally). It rewrites `hook.js:391` (the F2 comment), `test/ticket-marker-relay.test.js:439` and `docs/module-map.md:320` into the present tense. Comments and docs only; the assertion is unchanged. `grep -n "LIN-4240" hook.js test/ticket-marker-relay.test.js docs/module-map.md` now shows no "once/until … lands" wording.
- *Outside:* none on the ledger.

**Verified on what landed** (deployed commit `279dcb0a`): `tests/unit/session-telemetry.test.js` plus `tests/unit/decision-lifecycle-stamp-drift.test.js` pass 172/172 (witnesses 1–6), and the system test above passes 3/3.

**Not run:** no live production check. Harbour's page footer was not read, because the deployment record showed `success` for `279dcb0a` and I verified the behaviour on that exact commit instead.

**Accepted limits, unchanged.** A trailing `evidence` or `decision` entry still hides a park. This is documented in the docblock and was approved in the plan. The plan's "positive is-a-state-statement list" idea stays listed, not filed, because it needs a census of real feedback first.

**Housekeeping.** The description's "Approach" section was archived (snapshot captured 23:35:53Z and checked against the pre-prune text) and replaced with a stub. The problem statement, witnesses, stale-text list and acceptance criteria are kept. Siblings: LIN-4239's PR #326 is merged but the ticket still reads In Progress. Its Done gate is separate, so I left it. LIN-4233 gets a note.
